title: VoiceMem: Streaming Dual-Brain Memory for Real-Time Interaction

visual_explainer.blocker: A paper-specific mechanism figure has not yet passed grounded VISUAL_POLICY.md review; the verified bilingual deep note carries the mechanism, controls, and lifecycle caveats meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: VoiceMem separates factual and affect/persona state into parallel streaming memory paths and shows that the same upper memory layer can improve several interchangeable backends; its 134 ms figure is retrieval latency, not full response latency, and write/update lifecycle cost remains incomplete.
analysis.problem: Real-time speech agents need persistent factual memory, persona/affect continuity, and low-latency retrieval at once; text-only stores often flatten emotional evidence or require large candidate sets incompatible with streaming interaction.
analysis.core_idea: Use an informational 'left brain' for structured factual/entity memory and an emotional 'right brain' for persona/affect state, connect them through streaming read/write paths, and keep the upper memory layer decoupled from the underlying backend so retrieval can remain small-K and task-conditioned.

memory_design.write: Streaming interaction is parsed into factual/entity information and affect/persona evidence, which are written through separate informational and emotional paths; the project notes that extraction/tagging/graph writes are intentionally off the conversational critical path.
memory_design.organize: The informational path uses structured factual/entity memory while the emotional path maintains short-/long-horizon affect and persona nodes, including cross-entity relations rather than one flat text index.
memory_design.read: The runtime retrieves a small top-K set (default K=5) from the appropriate path and assembles it for the speech-language model; the paper reports 134 ms retrieval and about 430 memory tokens at K=5.
memory_design.update_forget: Streaming writes can update factual/persona structures asynchronously, but full consolidation, conflict repair, forgetting, privacy deletion, and long-term maintenance cost are not isolated.

compared_to: Classical memory backends such as Mem0 under much larger candidate counts
Persona-memory systems including MemOS under the same response model where available
The same Mem0, LangMem, and Zep backends with versus without the VoiceMem upper organization/routing layer
Text-only memory systems on the paper's long-form speech-memory benchmark
analysis.evidence: With top-5 retrieval the paper reports a factual average of 76.39 and substantial gains over larger-candidate classical memory systems. More diagnostic for mechanism portability, adding the same upper memory layer improves Mem0, LangMem, and Zep by +29.52, +15.76, and +22.92 points, raising their mean from 60.26 to 83.00 without replacing the backend. On persona evaluation with GPT-4o-mini, VoiceMem reports 74.16 versus 72.27 for MemOS; a separately fine-tuned responder reaches 76.56 and should not be treated as the same control. The system reports 134 ms dense dual-brain retrieval at K=5 and roughly 430 memory tokens.
analysis.why_it_matters: Multimodal conversational memory may need separate state contracts for factual truth and affect/persona continuity, while a thin upper routing/organization layer can be more portable than replacing the storage backend. Real-time constraints make candidate-set size and retrieval-path latency first-class evaluation objects.
limitations: The dual-brain package jointly changes extraction, representation, routing, graph structure, streaming I/O, and sometimes the responder, so component-level causal attribution is limited.
The reported 134 ms is memory retrieval latency within the streaming design, not end-to-end conversational response latency.
Write/extraction/tagging/graph maintenance is moved off the critical path but its full offline compute, dollar/energy cost, backlog behavior, and update consistency are not matched against baselines.
Some evaluation uses automated judges and a newly introduced speech-memory benchmark; annotation details and independent replication are limited.
